findings.reason: without a step that sets and verifies the staging root for imas-efit and nova, §4 runs its keep branch on exactly the 330 GB it was built to expire, so the plan's central outcome is not reached.
findings.text: §4 declares the staging root a per-project flight setting and says a symlink is kept and reported when its project has neither root set, but §6 has already replaced imas-efit's and nova's settled child folders with symlinks to `/work/projects/imas_gpu/crew-reports/<project>` and no section configures those projects' staging root (the field does not exist in code until s4 adds it, and §6 wrote no flight config); as written the sweep will classify every moved item as outside the permitted roots and keep it, so the backlog never expires on /work even though §6 and the `existing-backlog=move-then-expire` decision both promise it will

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `/reckon/crew-state-stays-bounded#s7` resolves (`id="s7"` at line 176 of that plan), and the cited `reckon/crew/gc.py` and `reckon/crew/routing.py` both exist; the extensionless hrefs are the house convention and resolve as `.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the s4 cases each assert a falsifiable outcome on a synthetic crew home, and three declared negative controls (drop the citation check, match only the item's own path, drop the target-root check) show the guard firing; the earlier gap on the 30-day ceiling is closed by the added "31-day-old item attributed to a plan that is still open is removed" case.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the host measure is committed to `docs/evidence/fragments/a-report-is-kept-only-when-persisted/an-unpersisted-report-expires.html` and the test lives under `tests/`, both durable paths.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags appear in the section's symbols or the new test filename, and its prose states the mechanism rather than a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the staging root is declared as a per-project flight setting but no section sets its value for the two projects whose backlog §6 already moved, so s4's own "neither root set → reported and kept" default keeps those moved copies forever.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s4 carries one deliverable (the retention sweep reaches the reports store); the expiry rule, attribution, keep set and symlink handling all serve that one measure.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s4 declares `depends-on: s2` (its keep rule reads §2 persist records) and s3/s5 declare `depends-on: s4`; every relationship resolves to a node that exists and points the right way.
